acceptance_criteria: `fn edge_length(&self, s: &Self::Shape, edge: SubShape) -> Result<f64, KernelError>` and `fn face_area(&self, s: &Self::Shape, face: SubShape) -> Result<f64, KernelError>` on `Kernel`, documented. `s` is unchanged.
A sub-shape of the wrong kind (a vertex or face for `edge_length`, a vertex or edge for `face_area`) and an index out of range are `KernelError::InvalidInput`, checked before the backend.

With `--features occt`, relative tolerance 1e-9 (sub-shapes found by `face_plane`, `sub_shape_bounding_box` or `work_axis_on`, not hard-coded indices): 1. Box [0,10]×[0,5]×[0,2]: edges along X, Y and Z give 10, 5 and 2; faces z = 2, y = 0 and x = 0 give 50, 20 and 10. The 6 face areas sum to `surface_area` of the box. 2. Cylinder r 5, h 10: the top circular edge gives 10π, the cylindrical face 100π, the top face 25π. 3. Sphere r 3: its one face gives 36π. 4. The box with its edge (0,5,2)–(10,5,2) chamfered 1 mm (`Kernel::chamfer`): the chamfer face gives 10√2. 5. Wrong kinds and an out-of-range index give `InvalidInput`.
Any new shim function catches all C++ exceptions, as the others do; any new `unsafe` is in `swx-kernel::ffi` with a comment.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and CI's `swx-kernel (occt)` job passes.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
